scoring_justification: Full recompute from raw phonon data (DFT+phonopy) is impossible in the verifier sandbox; consistent result‑level comparison against the paper’s published gold values is the strongest feasible verification.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold values for the acoustic phonon properties and lattice thermal conductivity listed in the paper’s Table 1.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Direct transcription from Table 1 of the paper (J. Mater. Chem. C, 2019, DOI:10.1039/c9tc04023d).
hidden_assets.generation_method: Copy‑pasted from the published PDF, retaining the same numbers and units.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the original computed values reported by the paper; they were not invented for the checker.

hidden_assets.purpose: Structural bounds for phonon spectral width and reduction percentages, derived from the paper’s qualitative descriptions.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: From the paper’s text: ‘spectrum width lowered by up to ~30% for Si, up to ~10% for Ge’ and approximate frequency range statements.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Illustrative plausible ranges were constructed from the paper’s own intervals; they are not arbitrary.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These bounds reflect the paper’s stated physical behaviour and would flag an entirely wrong computation.

outputs.description: Reproduced acoustic phonon properties and lattice thermal conductivity for all seven clathrate systems, corresponding to the quantities in the paper's Table 1.
Phonon spectrum widths for empty hosts and the filling-induced percentage reductions for filled systems.

output_contract.notes: All quantities are computed for the seven systems at 300 K where applicable. The checker scores table1_results.json by comparing the reported values to hidden paper-derived references within appropriate per-quantity tolerances. The spectral_width_report.json is scored by verifying that the reduction percentages fall within the physically expected ranges (Si-based: ~20–40%, Ge-based: ~5–15%) and that the empty-host widths are plausible.
